articles.title: Modi-Putin once again share a car ride post talks
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin met on Friday on the margins of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, according to an official readout from the Prime Minister's Office.This was their second meeting this year, following talks in Bishkek on the sidelines of the 26th SCO Summit on August 31, 2026.Putin had arrived in the capital earlier in the day and was welcomed upon arrival by Union Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh.The Thirukkural giftDuring the talks, PM Modi gifted Putin a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, the classical Tamil scripture composed by the weaver-saint Thiruvalluvar. "Two thousand years ago, Thiruvalluvar wrote the Thirukkural.It includes the entire gamut of human life. It has been translated into the Russian language. I am confident that the people-to-people contact will increase with the translation of the Thirukkural into Russian, which will play a big role in strengthening our relations," PM Modi told Putin.Also read: What is Thirukkural? 2,500-year-old ancient Tamil text written by poet Thiruvalluvar that PM Modi gifted to Vladimir Putin during BRICS SummitThe Thirukkural consists of 1,330 couplets, each two lines long, structured around three universal values — aram (virtue), porul (wealth and statecraft), and inbam (love). Revered by Tamils as a sacred scripture, it is often referred to as "the Tamil Veda".What the two leaders discussedAccording to the PMO, Modi and Putin reviewed progress in bilateral cooperation across political, economic, defence, energy, space, skill mobility and people-to-people domains. They welcomed Russia's International Industrial Exhibition "INNOPROM India", held for the first time in India from September 9-11, and underscored its importance in expanding trade and industrial ties between the two countries. The two leaders also visited the INNOPROM India exhibition together and interacted with participants.— ANI (@ANI) The leaders also exchanged views on India-Russia engagement in the multilateral sphere, particularly within BRICS under India's Chairship for 2026, and shared perspectives on regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region, which have affected maritime trade as well as the safety and security of Indian seafarers. PM Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remained the way forward in resolving these conflicts, and that India stood ready to assist in peace efforts.The two sides agreed to remain engaged in strengthening the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries further, noting that it continues to register significant growth and has shown resilience amid geopolitical uncertainties. President Putin also invited PM Modi to visit Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit, an invitation the Prime Minister accepted; the dates for the summit will be finalised through diplomatic channels.The INNOPROM visitINNOPROM, the International Industrial Exhibition, is a global platform bringing together manufacturers and buyers from around the world, offering a venue to showcase technologies, access international markets, and network on B2B opportunities. Its presence in India this year was part of the broader push to deepen India-Russia industrial ties.India's BRICS Chairship this year is guided by the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", with development, sustainability and innovation as key focus areas. BRICS has emerged as an important platform for coordination among major emerging economies and for advancing the interests of the Global South in multilateral institutions, with an agenda covering development, finance, technology, trade and people-to-people exchanges.Also read: Elephant, Dragon & Bear: Modi, Xi and Putin may converge at BRICS for a big power playThe grouping currently comprises 11 countries — Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE — which together account for around 49.5% of the global population, 40% of global GDP, and 26% of global trade, according to background information on India's 2026 Chairship. India's Chairship comes amid global economic fragmentation, technological disruption, geopolitical uncertainty, climate change and resource pressures.Friday's bilateral was Modi and Putin's second meeting this year and the latest in a continuing pattern of leader-level engagement between the two countries, including their meeting on the sidelines of the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek on August 31, 2026. The 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi is expected to bring together leaders and senior representatives from across the grouping over the two-day meeting starting Saturday.(With inputs from ANI)

articles.summary: Shares of One 97 Communications, the parent company of fintech major Paytm, rallied as much as 4% to Rs 1,804 after international brokerage Bernstein named the stock its top pick, citing robust merchant lending growth, operating leverage and the potential introduction of MDR on UPI as key drivers of earnings growth.With a target price of Rs 2,200, the brokerage forecasts an upside potential of up to 26% from current market levels. Even after excluding any potential impact from MDR on UPI, its FY29E EPS estimate stands at Rs 54, still above the Rs 46 consensus estimate.Why are Bernstein analysts bullish on Paytm shares?1.) Merchant loans are a key driver: Bernstein expects Paytm’s financial services revenue to grow at around 27% CAGR between FY26E and FY30E, driven primarily by its merchant loan distribution business. The brokerage expects merchant loans to remain the key contributor, accounting for around 75% of financial services revenue.Bernstein sees Paytm having a clear competitive advantage and a long runway for growth, even if the company only achieves modest increases in loan penetration among its merchant base.2.) Strong operating leverage: Analysts expect meaningful operating leverage from Paytm’s existing businesses, with indirect expenses projected to grow only around 8% as key cost drivers peak. Technology costs are expected to remain stable, while slower device additions should keep sales and merchant acquisition costs under control.Any incremental spending is likely to be directed towards new initiatives that can generate additional revenue.3.) MDR to boost profitability - Bernstein expects MDR on UPI to provide a meaningful boost to Paytm’s profitability. The brokerage points out that payment activity is highly concentrated, with around 4% of transactions accounting for 70% of transaction value, while the top 5% of merchants contribute the bulk of payment value.Given this concentration, Bernstein remains positive on the potential earnings upside for Paytm, regardless of how the eventual MDR framework is structured.Bernstein lists downside risks for Paytm stockMDR on UPI is not introduced: The estimates assume the introduction of MDR on UPI transactions, which accounts for 30% of our EBITDA forecasts. articles.title: UK chaos: Flights resume but delays ahead
articles.summary: Flights resumed at major UK airports on Wednesday after an air traffic control system failure cancelled more than 1,000 flights and caused delays across Britain. Heathrow and Gatwick warned that disruption could continue as airlines reposition aircraft and crew.Britain’s National Air Traffic Services (NATS) said it had resolved the problem in its flight processing system on Tuesday evening. However, delays continued across 15 UK airports and beyond as airlines and airports worked to clear a backlog of flights.Heathrow resumed departures but suspended arrivals for the rest of Tuesday night. The airport said flights were operating today, but warned that some disruption may continue.Gatwick also said its operations would take time to return to normal.“We still anticipate that it will take time for our operations to fully return to normal,” the airport said.Passengers were left stranded on aircraft, at terminals and at baggage collection areas during the disruption.British Airways cancelled or diverted more than 100 flights. The airline said aircraft and crew had ended up in different locations, affecting its operations.“The severity of the issue means there will be a significant knock-on impact,” a British Airways spokesperson said. “This incident was entirely out of our control and incredibly frustrating for our customers and colleagues, with aircraft and crews ending up out of place.”Passengers on a British Airways flight scheduled to fly from Heathrow to Baltimore spent four hours on the ground before leaving the aircraft. Cabin crew served pasta and chicken curry during the delay, while some passengers watched films or walked through the aisles.Passengers later reported confusion at the baggage claim area and said they were told to file claims for their bags.At Gatwick, Josie Donoghue spent three hours on a plane before her Ryanair flight to Ireland was cancelled.“Getting through that airport was like trying to get out of Alcatraz,” she said, referring to the former island prison in San Francisco Bay. “It’s just an absolute nightmare down there. It’s the only word I can use to describe it.”Ryanair said more than 65,000 passengers were affected and that it had cancelled more than 50 scheduled flights.EasyJet said some of its flights were “unable to operate” and that the system failure caused “delays to flights across Europe.”Other affected airports included London Stansted and London City, as well as airports in Manchester, Birmingham and Scotland. Passengers have been advised to check their flight status with their airline before travelling.
